verses.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
"Would a wise person answer with empty ideas and fill himself with the east wind?
Would he argue with useless talk and speeches that do no good?
You undermine reverence for God and discourage devotion to him.
Your guilt tells your mouth what to say, and you choose the words of people who scheme.
Your own mouth condemns you. Your own lips testify against you.
Were you the first person ever born? Did you come into the world before the hills?
Have you listened in on God's private counsel? Do you think wisdom belongs to you alone?
What do you know that we don't? What do you understand that we haven't grasped?
We have gray-haired men and elders among us who are much older than your father.
Is God's comfort too little for you, even when the words spoken to you are gentle?
Why do you let your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,
so that you turn your spirit against God and let these words out of your mouth?
How can a human being be clean? How can anyone born of a woman be righteous?
God doesn't even trust his holy ones. The heavens themselves aren't clean in his sight.
How much less someone corrupt and detestable, someone who drinks wrongdoing like water!
Listen to me and I'll show you. I'll tell you what I've seen,
what wise people learned from their ancestors and passed on without hiding it.
The land was given to those ancestors alone, and no foreigner passed among them.
A wicked person writhes in pain all his days, through all the years set aside for an oppressor.
Terrifying sounds fill his ears. While he's prospering, the destroyer comes upon him.
He doesn't expect to find his way back out of the darkness. A sword waits for him.
He wanders in search of bread, asking, 'Where is it?' He knows the day of darkness is close at hand.
Distress and anguish terrify him and overpower him like a king ready for battle.
He has raised his hand against God and acted arrogantly toward the Almighty.
He charges at God in defiance behind his thick shields.
His face is covered with fat, and his thighs have grown fat.
He has settled in deserted towns, in houses nobody lived in that were ready to collapse into heaps.
He won't stay rich, his wealth won't last, and his possessions won't spread over the land.
He won't escape the darkness. Flames will dry up his branches, and the breath of God's mouth will carry him away.
Let him stop fooling himself by trusting in emptiness. Emptiness is what he'll get in return.
His end will come before his time, and his branches will never turn green.
He'll drop his unripe grapes like a vine and shed his blossoms like an olive tree.
The company of the godless will bear no fruit, and fire will consume the tents of those who take bribes.
They conceive trouble and give birth to wrongdoing. In their hearts they prepare deceit."
